title: release.md frontmatter
description: Schema for the frontmatter of release.md, the canonical gating artifact for the launch phase — the last gate in this client's phase-graph, and the only required exit artifact of `launch`. Drafted by pr-review from its synthesized multi-agent review; approved by the release manager, never by the agent that drafted it. Clearing this gate is the end of a ticket's lifecycle here (there is no measure phase and no loop back to plan).

id.description: Ticket id this release traces back to — must match the id on the plan.md it was built from, and the ticket id recorded in the ticket's phase-state.json. An artifact carrying another ticket's id never satisfies this gate.

cycle.description: Always 1 in this client's phase-graph — there is no loop-back phase, so nothing ever seeds a cycle 2. Set it to 1; don't try to derive it.

pr_link.description: Link to the pull request this release covers. This is what makes the artifact auditable after the fact — the release manager approving it needs to be able to reach the actual diff, and so does whoever reads this in six months.

review_summary.description: The synthesized, deduped, severity-ranked result of the pr-review pass — which discipline reviewers ran, what they flagged, and what is blocking versus advisory. A summary here, the full findings in the body. Never a claim that the change was approved: pr-review synthesizes, the release manager decides.

rollout_plan.description: How this actually reaches production — all at once, behind a flag, staged by cohort/region, with which prerequisite migrations or config changes in which order.

rollback_plan.description: How this gets undone if it goes wrong, and how fast. A config flag flip and a revert-and-redeploy are very different answers; say which one this is. Anything touching production data, money movement, or a shared system needs a real answer here, not a formality.

verification.description: How launch success is actually checked once this is out — which dashboards, alerts, metrics or manual checks, over what window, and what result would mean this needs rolling back. This client has no measure phase; their own observability tooling covers what comes after, so this field is where the ticket says what to point it at.

open_questions.description: Anything unresolved before this can ship. Must be empty, or explicitly waived by the release manager, before launch can close.

source_docs.description: Carried forward from plan.md (and through it from spec.md/scope.md/intent.md) — the PRD/RFC this release traces back to, if any

approved_by.description: Required when status is approved — the release manager (phase-graph.yaml's approval role for launch), distinct from the author when enforce_segregation_of_duties is on. pr-review drafts this artifact and must never fill this field in itself.

approval_evidence.description: Required when status is approved (require_approval_evidence in phase-graph.yaml) — a link to the Jira comment/Slack message/email/change-record where the release manager actually approved this. A release manager typically approves in a change-management system, not in git; this is what ties approved_by to a real, checkable event.

approvals.description: One entry per approving role. Only needed when this artifact's gate asks for more than one signature (a quorum or tier strategy in .pdlc/phase-graph.yaml). A single-approver gate keeps using status/approved_by/approval_evidence. Every entry needs its own evidence link when require_approval_evidence is on — one link does not cover two people.

role.description: The approval role named by this gate in .pdlc/phase-graph.yaml, e.g. product_owner. An entry for a role the gate did not ask for does not count toward it.

by.description: The person who decided. Required when status is approved.

evidence.description: Link to where this person actually approved or declined — the Jira comment, Slack message or change record.
